description: zeptoclaw has Android device shell blocklist bypass via argument permutation
how_introduced: AI-authored code contributed directly: commit 8f1c1db4f3e6d9e0beb16dc69bf07b10f12276cc, generated with Claude Code and co-authored by Claude Opus 4.6, introduced the Android `device_shell()` feature and its vulnerable substring-based blocklist. That code accepted arbitrary `shell` commands and only looked for literal `"rm -rf"` / `"rm -r"`, missing equivalent recursive-delete forms such as `rm -fr`, `rm -f -r`, and `rm --recursive --force`.

bug_commits.author: qhkm
bug_commits.message: fix: harden Android tool correctness and security (#92)

agent_verdicts.reasoning: This commit added `src/tools/android/actions.rs` and introduced `device_shell()`, which normalized the user-supplied command and then blocked only literal substrings like `"rm -rf"` and `"rm -r"` via `lower.contains(pattern)`. That is exactly the vulnerable design the fix replaced with flag-aware parsing, because semantically equivalent forms such as `rm -fr`, `rm -f -r`, and `rm --recursive --force` do not contain either literal substring. `git log` for `src/tools/android/actions.rs` shows only this introduction commit and the fix, and pickaxe searches for `"rm -rf"` and `pub async fn device_shell` both trace the origin to 8f1c1db4f3e6d9e0beb16dc69bf07b10f12276cc.
